secondary.author: Paul Cartledge
secondary.rationale: Paul Cartledge is a distinguished historian of ancient Greece, and this book offers a comprehensive and modern scholarly assessment of Alexander's life and legacy.

secondary.title: Alexander the Great
secondary.author: Robin Lane Fox
secondary.rationale: While slightly before the 1976 cutoff, Robin Lane Fox's biography is considered a seminal work and remains highly influential in Alexander scholarship. It is often cited and discussed in later works.

secondary.title: The Campaigns of Alexander
secondary.author: Arrian
secondary.rationale: Arrian's 'Anabasis Alexandri' is one of the most important and reliable ancient sources for Alexander's military campaigns. While not a modern secondary source, it is a primary source that is essential for any scholarly research on Alexander and is widely available in translation.

suggestions.notes: Direct primary sources authored by Alexander the Great himself (letters, speeches) are extremely scarce and often of questionable authenticity or only preserved in fragments within later historical accounts. Therefore, no direct primary sources authored by him are listed. Arrian's 'The Campaigns of Alexander' is included as a crucial ancient primary source that is foundational to modern scholarship.
